Lessons.Title: Weight and Capacity Measurements
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will apply your understanding of multiplicative comparison and unit conversion to solve multi-step problems about weight and capacity.
In earlier lessons, you were introduced to several units of weight and capacity (kilograms, grams, pounds, ounces, liters, and milliliters). In this lesson, you solve problems involving the units of capacity you worked with in grade 3. You use your knowledge of unit conversion and multiplicative reasoning to solve multi-step problems.
Core relationship: Mass and capacity measurement problems. Convert to milliliters or grams before multi-step addition/subtraction.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:   Number Talk: Lots of Thousands	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Milk and Mango Lassi	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Clay for Art Class	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  More Clay	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: How many milliliters are in 2 L 300 mL?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): A 3-L bottle loses 750 mL. How much remains?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mass and capacity measurement problems
KeyConcepts.Rule: Convert to milliliters or grams before multi-step addition/subtraction.
KeyConcepts.Example: How many milliliters are in 2 L 300 mL?

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact source-goal relationship
KeyConcepts.Definition: US customary capacity uses 1 gallon=4 quarts and 1 quart=4 cups.
KeyConcepts.Rule: US customary capacity uses 1 gallon=4 quarts and 1 quart=4 cups.

KeyConcepts.Title: Independent check or representation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Weight uses 1 pound=16 ounces; do not mix mass and capacity.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Weight uses 1 pound=16 ounces; do not mix mass and capacity.

WorkedExamples.Title: Edulytics source-goal mathematical model 1
WorkedExamples.Question: How many cups equal 2 gallons?
WorkedExamples.Method: US customary capacity uses 1 gallon=4 quarts and 1 quart=4 cups.
Steps: One gallon has 4 quarts×4 cups=16 cups.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Mixing liters and milliliters without conversion.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Convert to milliliters or grams before multi-step addition/subtraction.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Converting a gallon directly to four cups.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The reasoning does not preserve the task's mathematical quantities or representation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: One gallon has four quarts, hence sixteen cups.
